# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Seed iteration (no prior iterations). Capability under edit: the agent system prompt (`prompt.md`).
I read the adapter (`.capevolve/project/adapters/adapter.py`) and the vendored scorer
(`third_party/spreadsheetbench/evaluation/evaluation.py`) to ground every edit in how grading
actually works — not to edit them.

## Two grading facts that ground the whole iteration (from source, not guesswork)
1. **The agent's final code is re-run on 2 HIDDEN input files.** adapter.py ~L933: after case 1
   is solved, `solution = last_code.replace(input_file.name, case_input.name)` and the output name
   is rewritten `1_<id>_output.xlsx`→`2_/3_`, then re-executed. The 3 test cases share the same
   `answer_position` range but have DIFFERENT data. So code tuned to the visible sample fails cases 2/3.
2. **The scorer (`compare_cell_value`/`transform_value`) compares by exact Python TYPE, only on
   `.value`.** `if type(v1)!=type(v2): return False`. Numbers→`round(float,2)`, datetimes→day serial,
   numeric strings coerced to float (so "5"==5) but date-strings are NOT coerced (text date ≠ real date).
   Fill/font-color and (implicitly) number-format comparisons are commented out — only cell VALUES matter.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Overfit to visible sample / hardcoded output | 5192, 3911, 38332, 39046, +truncation in 110-2/325-44/450-9 | Agent doesn't know code is re-run on hidden inputs; writes constants/answers from the preview or instruction examples | KNOWLEDGE | grading-mechanism disclosure + no-hardcode rule |
| 2 | Value TYPE / date-type mismatch | 50630, 30709 (partial) | Agent can't derive that grader compares by exact type; writes text where a real date/number is expected | KNOWLEDGE | explicit type contract |
| 3 | Answer expressed as non-graded formatting | CF_11072 | Agent spent the answer on fill colors, which are not compared | KNOWLEDGE | "only values graded" fact |
| 4 | No inspect/generalize/verify before finishing | 5192, 3911, 38332 | Behavioral: writes final code without checking data/type | STRUCTURE | pre-save numbered checklist |
| — | Complex Sheet-Level algorithm correctness | 110-2, 325-44, 450-9 | Idiosyncratic wrong algorithm (not a shared prose-fixable gap) | (skipped) | partly helped by #1/#4 |
| — | Infra: formula recalc failed | 73-45 | Environment (LibreOffice recalc failed on 3/3) — flagged INFRASTRUCTURE by scorer | (skipped, env) | none |

## Changes made this iteration (one edit block, 4 additive knowledge/structure additions; existing 6 rules kept verbatim)
| cluster | edit class | file | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | KNOWLEDGE (missing rule) + reality disclosure | prompt.md "How your code is graded" | States code is re-run on hidden inputs with different data; forbids hardcoding; requires data-driven logic over real extent. General policy, no task specifics | Yes — 24 passers already write general code (41297/44266/52021…) so behavior unchanged |
| 2 | KNOWLEDGE (output contract) | prompt.md type bullet | Write dates as real datetime, numbers as numbers; grader compares by type, rounds numbers to 2dp, dates to day; anchor to sample/adjacent type | Yes — passers already emit matching types; anchored to observed data, not a blanket flip |
| 3 | KNOWLEDGE (missing fact) | prompt.md "only values graded" bullet | Colors/formats/formula-text not compared; put answer in values; formula OK only if it evaluates correctly | Yes — colors were never graded; formula-writers (52021/46897/55060/55667/58109) still valid |
| 4 | STRUCTURE (pre-finish checklist) | prompt.md "Before you save" | 5-item precondition list making generalize + type-check + range-only unavoidable before save | Yes — passers already satisfy every item |

## Verify-the-fix (trace → what the edit changes)
- 5192 (`ws['B2']='1456CH02'` — pasted the instruction's own example strings): rule "never hardcode / paste an example; compute from cell data" → agent parses col A and applies the "move last number to front" transform generally. Passers write general code, unaffected.
- 3911 (hand-computed `allocation=[[5,0,...]]` literal): same no-hardcode rule → computes the note distribution from actual salary cells; would work on cases 2/3.
- 38332 (`ws['D{r}']=1` for all rows): no-hardcode + "don't fill a fixed constant that was right for the rows you saw" → counts distinct occurrences from col A per row.
- 50630 / 30709 (date cells): type contract "dates must be real datetime objects" → ensures date type matches; 30709 already wrote datetime so this is reinforcing.
- CF_11072 ("highlight closer value", agent applied green fills + wrote guess text): "only VALUES graded, colors not compared" → directs the answer into cell values instead of fills.
- Blast radius: all 4 additions are ADDITIVE (new sections) with the original 6 rules kept verbatim; each matches what the 24 passing tasks already do (general data-driven code, matching types, literal paths — verified all 24 use `1_<id>_input`), so BOUNDED. No global decision/permission rule was loosened; the soft "prefer literal values" line was NOT strengthened into a formula ban, precisely because 5 passing tasks write formulas and pass via recalc.

## Process & features used
- Subagents/worktrees: not used — serial diagnosis was faster here (small trace set; the key evidence was in the adapter + scorer source, read directly).
- Prior iterations: none exist (this is the seed); LEDGER/JOURNAL/RUNMAP empty.

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)
- Do NOT ban formulas / force literals globally: tasks 52021, 46897, 55060, 55667, 58109 pass by writing formulas that LibreOffice recalculates. A formula ban would regress them.
- The two grading facts above (hidden re-run; type-exact value-only compare) are the backbone — keep them stated.
- Keep the original 6 rules (range restriction, error-recovery) intact.

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why)
- 73-45: scorer flagged INFRASTRUCTURE (formula recalc failed on all 3 cases) — environment fault, not a prompt defect; handed back, not optimized.
- 110-2, 325-44, 450-9: complex Sheet-Level algorithms whose failure is wrong transformation logic specific to each task, not a shared knowledge gap prose can fix without hardcoding an answer. The generalization (#1) + checklist (#4) edits reduce the truncation/`rows[:9]` sub-failures but I did not add task-specific prose (would overfit / fail the REAL+SAFE tests).
